title: overrides.yaml (curation_version 3)
description: Manual curation applied after fetch, before cleaning. The build validates overrides.yaml against this schema (ingest/curation.py) before applying anything, so this file is the complete reference for what may be written. Dates are ISO: unquoted YYYY-MM-DD reads as a date in YAML. Rules a schema can't express (when as_of may be omitted, whether a milestone date fits its order, keys sorted within each section) are checked in ingest/curation.py.

curation_version.description: The format of this file. 3 is the only one the build reads; tools/migrate_curation.py converts version 2.

overrides.description: Edit fields on an order ALREADY in the orders sheet, keyed by username (case-insensitive), or username#2 (#3, ...) for one of a user's several orders. Only the fields given are changed.

additions.description: Append an order NOT in the sheet (forum-only), keyed by username. Give what has been reported; a field left out is unknown and charts as Unknown.

deletions.description: Drop entries that no longer exist (a cancellation, a superseded resubmission), per sheet.

orders.description: Rows of the orders sheet, keyed by username.

reservations.description: Rows of the reservations sheet, keyed by username.

verified.description: Values that look like entry errors but have been confirmed, so the checks in ingest/outliers.py stop setting them aside. Keyed by username.

iso_month.description: A month, when only the month is known: YYYY-MM.

unknown.description: Known to be unknown: replaces what the sheet says with no value.

loose_date.description: A day, a month, or unknown.

source.description: Where the information came from: a forum URL, or text starting with 'inferred' for a judgment made from the data itself (inferred — <why>). A list when there are several.

as_of.description: When we learned it: the post, or the curation date. Anchors the stale-override check, which compares later sheet changes against it. Required, except on an entry whose only dates are milestones (vin_assigned, delivery_scheduled) and which sets nothing else.

checked.description: A later date on which someone re-checked the entry against the sheet and it still holds. The stale-override check then only counts changes after it.

reason.description: A short note, shown with the entry in the report.

delivery.description: The delivery estimate, in one of the forms the delivery parser produces.

oneOf.description: month: some time in that month.
window: a number of weeks (or days), or a span of them, counted from the order date, or from `from` when the estimate was given later.

from.description: The date the window counts from, when not the order date: 'they told me 2-4 more weeks' on this day.

dates.description: The order's dates. resv_date, order_date and delivery are its values; vin_assigned and delivery_scheduled are milestones, when its FINAL VIN and FINAL delivery date took hold (#99), from a post saying when. Without a milestone, it is the first snapshot that showed the final value; one that can't fit (before the order, after the sheet already showed the value, ...) is listed, not used.

vin_assigned.description: When the final VIN was assigned.

delivery_scheduled.description: When the final (firm) delivery date was set.

config.description: The build, in the sheet's own wording (see dimensions.yaml for each column's categories).

tow.description: Tow package: Yes, No or Included.

spare.description: Compact spare: Yes, No or Included.

fields.description: What an order entry may set, besides its dates and config.

vin.description: The VIN as reported: the sequence number, or a partly hidden one (123XX), or a word (TBD, unknown). Quoted, so a leading zero survives. It goes through the same VIN recovery as the sheet.

location.description: State or province, as the sheet writes it (CA, Canada - British Columbia).

match.description: Field -> value, scoping a deletion to the ONE entry it names; every field must match. A username is not a stable key for an order, so prefer a match: a later order under the same name then fails it and the stale deletion is reported, instead of silently removing the new order.

deletion.description: A removal. The reason is shown in the data-quality panel; nothing in the data marks a cancellation, so the forum post is the evidence.

verified.description: Confirmed values the entry-error checks would otherwise set aside.
